info.description:
Read-only, cacheable, versioned REST API over cars-data.com's multilingual
vehicle catalogue (103,099 variants, 1,300+ models, 5,395 generations,
224 spec types, 20 languages).

# Two tiers, and only two

There is **no free tier**. Access to this API comes in exactly two shapes,
and the difference between them is not a quota — it is which data exists
behind the key.

## 1. Demo — self-serve, free, 40 cars

Fill in the request form (`POST /keys/demo`; every field is required),
click the link in the email, and the key is active. Nothing waits for a
human.

A demo key is scoped to a **frozen sample of 40 cars** — 5 brands x 2
models x 2 generations x 2 variants, covering all 10 fuel types — with
**every** spec, every image and all 20 languages. `GET /demo` hands over
the whole set in one call, so there is nothing to discover by probing.

**The demo cannot reach the catalogue, structurally.** This is not a quota
and not an allowlist consulted per route: a request carrying a demo key is
dispatched, before any catalogue route runs, into a separate router
(`src/routes/demo.ts`) that answers entirely from a pre-rendered blob in
Workers KV. That module and the set it serves (`src/lib/demo-set.ts`)
contain zero references to Hyperdrive or to Postgres — there is no code
path from a demo request to a database connection. A leaked demo key
therefore cannot be used to walk the catalogue, because the catalogue is
not reachable from where that key is answered, no matter how many requests
it makes. Anything outside the 40 cars answers `403`, never `404`: the
route exists, the tier does not reach it.

## 2. Paid

Two products, both arranged by hand — there is no instant checkout:

  * **The Apify Actor** — the API over the full catalogue, metered and
    billed per result by Apify's own platform:
    https://apify.com/carsdatacom/car-specs-api
  * **A licensed data export** — the modules you need, as CSV and JSON
    with a field dictionary and a per-field coverage sheet, with an
    optional update subscription. Priced and ordered on
    https://cars-data.com/en/api

`GET /export` is **not** that export and never serves bulk data; it
answers `403` with a pointer to the licensing page.

# Conventions

  * Every success is `{ data, meta }`, plus `links` on paginated lists.
    `meta.last_synced_at` is on every response.
  * Every error is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.
  * Identifiers are **opaque tokens**, not integers: `v_1a2b3c4d` for a
    variant, `g_…` for a generation, `m_…` for a model, `c_…` for a
    pagination cursor. They are domain-separated — a variant token is
    refused where a model token is expected — and an unparseable token
    gets the same `404` as a car that does not exist. Only the `apify`
    plan receives raw integer ids, because the published Actor's input
    schema declares `variantId` as an integer.
  * Attribution is required; see the Terms of Service.

Identical behaviour to `POST /keys/demo`, same request body, same
responses. It exists so a cached page or a copied `curl` line posting
here keeps working.

**It does not issue a reviewed key.** Until 2026-10-06 this endpoint
recorded a request that a human approved by hand, and the key it
eventually produced reached the whole catalogue. That tier is gone:
nothing self-serve reaches the catalogue any more, so there is nothing
left to review.

post.description:
Step 1 of 2. Records the request and emails a one-click activation
link. **No key exists yet** and nothing is pending review — the link is
the only gate, and it is yours to click.

Every field is required. They are not a review gate; they are the
lead, and asking for them after issuing would mean nobody fills them
in.

Limits: 5 requests per IP per day, one key per email address. The
email domain is checked for an MX record, because a key emailed to a
domain that cannot receive mail helps nobody.
